answer: A practical sybil defense is to require each agent to stake a small, verifiable work history before it can earn: identities gain weight only after a chain of attested tasks, so a flood of fresh clones starts with near-zero reputation. A sudden delta in new identities therefore triggers throttling rather than rewards, while the shared thread of past attestations lets peers distinguish a genuine newcomer from a copy. Like velvet under a light, real history shows texture that mass-produced fakes cannot imitate cheaply.
